name: resizable
behavior: APG window splitter pattern: the handle is role=separator with aria-orientation, aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow (the primary panel's size as a percentage), aria-valuetext and aria-controls naming that panel. The handle is in the tab order. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (ArrowUp/ArrowDown when the split is horizontal) move it by one step, Shift+Arrow by a larger step, Home/End move it to its limits, and Enter toggles between collapsed and the last size. Pointer dragging and keyboard must reach exactly the same positions.

parts.note: the panel group; sets the split axis
one resizable region; a panel may itself contain a nested group

parts.statesNote: the painted rule is a hairline but the hit area is widened to target-min; dragging takes border-strong and layer-overlay per states.md

parts.note: the visible dot/bar affordance on the handle; aria-hidden

anatomyNotes: Intersection of shadcn Resizable (react-resizable-panels: Group/Panel/Separator) and Salt's react-resizable-panels-theme, which themes the very same library — so the parts coincide exactly and the difference is entirely recipe (handle thickness, grip presence, hover colour). Salt's own SplitLayout/ParentChildLayout are static layouts with no draggable separator and are therefore NOT this component. orientation names the SPLIT axis: orientation=horizontal means panels sit side by side and the handle is vertical — the handle's own aria-orientation is the perpendicular value, which the behavior contract fixes so themes cannot disagree.
